div.l: Than wold he speke and crie as he were wood
And whan he had wel drunke the wyne
Than̄ wold he speke no word but latyn̄
A fewe termes had he tuo or thre
That he had lerned out of som decre
No wonder was he herd it all the day
And eke I knewe well that a Iay
Cam wel clepe watte as doth a Pope
But who so coude in othir thing him grope
That than than had he spent all his philosophie
Ay Questioque Iuris wolde he crie
He was a gentill harlott and a kynde
A better felawe shuld a man̄ nat fynde
He wold suffre for a quart of wyn
A good felawe to haue his concubyne
A twelmonth and excuse him ate fulle
Full priuelich a fynche couthe he pulle
And if he fond any where a good felawe
He wold teche him to haue non awe
In such caas of the Archediacons curse
But yef a mannes soule were in his purs
For be his purs he shuld I punisshed be
Purs is the Archediacons helle quod he
But wel I wot he lyed riȝt in dede
Of cursing ouȝt eueri man to drede
For curs will sle lik as a soiling saueth
And also war him of a Significauit
In daunger had he at his ougne guise
The yong gerles of the diocise
And knew ther counseill ⁊and was of her reed
A garlond had he sett vpon his hed
As gret as it were for an ale stake
A Bokeler had he made him of a cake
With him rod there a gentil Pardoner
Of Rouncyvale his frend ⁊and his comper
That streit was come from the court of Rome
Full loude he sang come hider loue to me
This Sompnoᵘur bar to him a stif burdoıı̄un
Was neuer trompe of all so gret a soun
This Pardoner had heer as yelwe as wex
But smothe it henge as doth a strik of flex
Be ounces heng his lockes that he hadde
And therwith his shuldres ouerspradde
But thinne it lay be colpons oon by oon̄
But hood for iolyte were he non̄
For trussed vp in his walett
Him thouȝt he rod al of the newe get
Thus saf his cappe he rod al bare
Such glaryng yhen had he as an hare
A vernicle had he sowed vpon his cappe
His walett beforn̄ him in his lappe
But ful of pardoıı̄un com from Rome al hoot
A vois he had as small as is a goat
No berde had he ne neuer shuld haue
As smothe it was as it were late I shaue
I trowe he were a gelding or a mare
But of his craft from Berwik vnto ware
Ne was ther such an othir Pardoner
For in his male he had a pilwe bere
Wich that he said was oure Lady seall
He seid he had a gobett of the seall
That seint Petir had whan that he went
Vpon the see till Ihu crist him hent
He had a cros of laton full of stones
And in a glas he had pigges bones
But with these reliques whan that he fonde
A poore Person duelling vpon̄ londe
Vpon a day he gat him more money
Than the person gat in monthes twey
And thus with feined flatery and Iapes
He made the person and people his apes
But truli to telle ate laste
In the chirche he was a noble ecclesiaste
Wel coude he rede a lesson or a story
But alderbest he sang an offretory
For wel he wist whan was that song
He must preche and wel fyle his tonge
To winne siluer if he wel couthe
Therfore he sang the merilier and loude
Now haue I tolde you shortli in a clause
The stat the array the ombre and eke the cause
Whi that assembled was this companie
In Southwerk at this gentil hostelrie
That hight the Tabard fast beside the welle
But now is tyme for you for to telle
Hou that we beren vs thilke niȝt
Whan we were in that hoist aliȝt
And aftir woll I telle of oure viage
